identity.title: Boxes Inside Boxes: Tag Nesting
identity.description: Learn the Russian nesting doll rule: child tags must close before their parent tags.

primaryCapability.statement: Identify properly nested parent-child HTML elements and detect illegal tag overlaps.

knows: Buttons and headings are created with opening and closing tags
A closing tag uses a forward slash
likelyMisconceptions: Tags can close in any order regardless of which tag opened first

canDo: Nest child tags inside parent tags following the last-opened, first-closed rule.

learning.targetMentalModel: Russian nesting dolls: you cannot put the lid on the outer doll before closing the inner doll.

experience.startingState: Learner knows standalone tags, now combining them into hierarchies.
experience.narrativeContext: Closing tags out of order forces the browser parser to guess your intent.
experience.primaryInteraction: Selecting properly nested markup and assembling parent-child pairs.
experience.expectedOutcome: Learner enforces proper tag nesting without cross-boundary overlaps.

activities.title: The Russian Doll Rule
activities.instruction: Tags inside tags must close before their parents do.

content.title: The Russian Doll Rule
content.hook: You can't close the outer doll before putting the lid on the inner one. HTML works the exact same way.
content.context: When you put a button inside a paragraph, finish the inner tag before closing the outer one.
goals: Spot valid nesting versus illegal overlaps
Assemble properly nested parent and child tags

activities.title: What does the browser do if you close tags out of order?
activities.instruction: Think about how browser parsers handle imperfect HTML:

hints.text: Browsers are designed to never show raw crash screens to users.

content.question: What does the browser do if you close tags out of order?

options.text: It tries to auto-repair your markup by guessing what you meant.
It crashes the webpage with a fatal red error screen.
It deletes the tags and turns the whole page into plain text.

content.explanation: Browsers are forgiving: when tags overlap, the HTML parser guesses how to fix your DOM tree, often causing strange layout glitches.

feedback.correct: Exactly. The browser guesses, and its guess rarely matches what you wanted.
feedback.incorrect: Browsers never crash on bad HTML. They guess and patch the tree behind your back.

content.title: Nesting Rules Mastered
takeaways: Last opened, first closed: child tags must terminate before parent tags.
Tags cannot overlap like crossed sticks — they nest like Russian dolls.
When tags overlap, the browser guesses your intent, usually causing layout bugs.
nextSteps: Next up: Void elements — the few tags that don't need a closing tag.
